title: Neural-model optimization improves tested silver-carp oil extraction
summary: An ANN-guided search selected extraction conditions for silver-carp viscera oil, followed by physical confirmation. The measured yield was 79.44%, compared with 76.68% at a response-surface-selected setting. This is a small process-optimization experiment; separate encapsulation improvements were not shown to be AI-selected.
ai_technology: Multilayer perceptron with genetic-algorithm search over its learned response surface
organization: China Agricultural University; Mississippi State University

evidence.tested: The ANN learned from 17 response-surface-design experiments, with 70/15/15 training/test/validation allocation and a three-input, ten-hidden-node architecture selected through trials. Its learned response served as the genetic-search fitness function. The selected setting predicted 82.45% extraction; follow-up measurements yielded 79.44%, versus 76.68% for the response-surface setting, with source-reported significant difference.
evidence.unknown: Seventeen training-design runs produce very small evaluation subsets, and architecture choice by trial/error limits generalization claims. The physical optimized-setting measurement is distinct from the reported high fit correlation; its 79.44% yield is below the 82.45% prediction. The result concerns one byproduct/process system rather than universal extraction efficiency. Gelatin/coacervation optimization, capsule stability and simulated digestion are separate conventional downstream experiments, so they are not credited as additional AI-guided discoveries.
evidence.ai_role: A learned nonlinear extraction-response model actively supplied the search objective for a newly tested process setting, rather than only fitting previously measured yields.

source_review.scope: Original ANN/search construction,17-experiment comparison/validation Methods and represented extraction Results actually read; later microencapsulation claims not attributed to learned optimization.
